QuestionStmt.S: The point of intersection of the diagonals of the rectangle whose sides are contained in the lines $x = 8, x = 10, y = 11$ and $y = 12$ is

Solution.S:
The four sides of the rectangle are vertical lines x = 8 and x = 10, and horizontal lines y = 11 and y = 12. Thus the vertices are A(8,11), B(10,11), C(10,12), D(8,12).

Diagonal AC joins A(8,11) and C(10,12). Its equation using two-point form:
$$\frac{y-11}{12-11} = \frac{x-8}{10-8} \Rightarrow \frac{y-11}{1} = \frac{x-8}{2} \Rightarrow 2(y-11) = x-8 \Rightarrow x - 2y + 14 = 0.$$

Diagonal BD joins B(10,11) and D(8,12):
$$\frac{y-11}{12-11} = \frac{x-10}{8-10} \Rightarrow \frac{y-11}{1} = \frac{x-10}{-2} \Rightarrow -2(y-11) = x-10 \Rightarrow x + 2y - 32 = 0.$$

Solving the two equations: Adding gives 2x - 18 = 0 → x = 9. Substitute into x + 2y - 32 = 0 → 9 + 2y - 32 = 0 → 2y = 23 → y = 23/2.

Thus the intersection point is (9, 23/2), which matches option B.
